finite_source_aware_pronunciation_adjudi.raw_primary_sentence_transcript: Since January 2023, customer service employment is down about 10% and administrative assistance about 15%.
finite_source_aware_pronunciation_adjudi.raw_secondary_sentence_transcript: Since January 2023, customer service employment is down about 10% and administrative assistance about 15%.
finite_source_aware_pronunciation_adjudi.scope_limit: This source, input, native sentence and whole native waveform only. All other words and numerical values retain exact independent ordered coverage. No general normalization rule maps assistance to assistants.
finite_source_aware_pronunciation_adjudi.lexical_identity_basis: The exact canonical source and actual literal speech input fix the intended lexical noun assistants. Primary research permits overlapping American /ns/ and /nts/ surface realizations, so ASR assistance alone does not establish a lexical substitution. This finite decision accepts that natural source-word realization, not an alternative word or a claim that underlying dictionary forms are identical.

primary_sources.authors: Isaiah WonHo Yoo and Barbara Blankenship
primary_sources.title: Duration of epenthetic [t] in polysyllabic American English words
primary_sources.journal: Journal of the International Phonetic Association 33(2),153-164
primary_sources.precision: Publisher abstract; seven American speakers, controlled sentences; independent TIMIT comparison.
primary_sources.finding: Word-final position favors stop insertion in /ns/. Underlying and inserted stop closure durations did not differ significantly in the controlled experiment, while underlying stops were significantly longer in TIMIT.
primary_sources.limitation: This studies epenthesis and duration, not a universal merger; it does not directly test the exact assistants/assistance pair or this recording.

primary_sources.author: Caroline L.Smith
primary_sources.title: The effect of allophonic patterns on consonant cluster simplification in American English
primary_sources.precision: pp1-3, sections1.1,2,3.2; Buckeye corpus, 40 Columbus Ohio speakers; 543 /nts/ tokens and 660 /ns/ tokens.
primary_sources.finding: The original corpus analysis documents /nts/ stop deletion and /ns/ stop insertion. Re-timing may acoustically hide an articulated consonant. The own-data /ns/ insertion rate is 13%, lower than controlled studies.
primary_sources.limitation: The paper does not identify assistants/assistance as an experimental pair. Its cited TIMIT14% deletion figure belongs to earlier Blankenship research, not this original corpus result; no such percentage is generalized here.
